subject: EU/UK data transfer pathway: SCCs options, risks and timeline
messages:
From: Tom Gilbert <tgilbert@northridgehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T09:12:00+01:00
Subject: SCCs path for Northridge - what do you recommend?

Hi Laura / Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement at Northridge (cc'd Leah) have started the legal checklist and asked us to confirm two things by EOD Friday:

1) Which SCCs module Redwood is planning to sign (processor→controller / processor→processor / controller→processor variant) for the services in scope.
2) Whether you anticipate needing a UK-specific transfer instrument (we've been asked if the UK Transfer Addendum or an alternative is required).

They also asked for a short summary of operational mitigations (region pinning, subprocessor list, logging/audit evidence) and an estimated legal signoff timeline. Can you confirm next steps and share any draft docs we can pass to procurement?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement wants to present to their board on 04-Jun.

Cheers,
Tom
Head of IT Procurement
Northridge Health

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Tom Gilbert <tgilbert@northridgehealth.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:03:00+01:00
Subject: RE: SCCs path for Northridge - what do you recommend?

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. Short answer up front: we recommend a dual-track approach that is low-friction for procurement and preserves operational controls. Details below and I attach a concise checklist and draft of a UK transfer addendum.

Recommended path (summary):
- Primary instrument: Standard EU SCCs (controller-processor template) configured to match our Processor obligations. For the customer-facing flow we map this to the Processor→Controller variant in the attached module comparison so procurement sees exact clause correspondence.
- Parallel UK coverage: provide a short UK Transfer Addendum (UTA) to address post-Brexit wording differences and the ICO's guidance. The UTA is intentionally lightweight — it mirrors the SCCs protections and points to the same security and audit commitments.

Why this route:
- Single SCCs instrument alone often triggers additional procurement queries about the UK's adequacy decision and residual differences; the UTA removes ambiguity and speeds signoff.
- Operational mitigations (region pinning, limited subprocessor list for the production tenant, SOC2 evidence + audit logs) are documented and linked in the checklist.

What I'm attaching for procurement:
- SCCs-module-comparison-Redwood-v1.xlsx (mapping matrix, clause-by-clause)
- UK-Transfer-Addendum-draft-v2.docx (editable draft)
- SCCs-checklist-rollout.pdf (timeline, owners, evidence items)

Timeline proposal:
- Legal review & redlines from Northridge: 5 business days
- Redwood legal review of redlines: 3 business days
- Exec signoff & DocuSign circulation: 2 business days
=> Target: fully executed within ~2 weeks after we receive procurement redlines. If procurement wants an accelerated path we can pre-populate the CTA (consolidated transfer addendum) and start DocuSign while redlines are discussed.

Action items for Tom / Leah:
- Leah: please share any procurement redlines in a tracked Word file so we can incorporate directly.
- Tom: confirm whether Northridge requires a single instrument (SCCs only) for the board pack or if the dual instrument approach is acceptable — that affects whether we send the UTA in parallel or hold it until after their board decision.

Markus & Rishi — tagging you for legal nuance & pricing impact notes.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SCCs-module-comparison-Redwood-v1.xlsx; UK-Transfer-Addendum-draft-v2.docx; SCCs-checklist-rollout.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Gilbert <tgilbert@northridgehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T11:20:00+01:00
Subject: RE: SCCs path for Northridge - what do you recommend?

Laura — good summary. A couple of legal clarifications we should surface for procurement to avoid late asks: 

1) Module choice: rather than framing it as a single "processor→controller" label, call out the exact clause references and the data flow assumptions we used in the mapping matrix. Procurement teams sometimes conflate the module heading with the operational scope; the matrix removes that ambiguity.

2) UK nuance: the UTA should explicitly reference the ICO's post-Brexit explanatory notes (we include a footnote in v2). Keep the UTA additive (mirrors SCCs) rather than substitutive — that reduces negotiation.

3) Fallback controls: if the customer insists on minimizing cross-border transfers, offer an alternative priced option: region-locked hosting + restricted KV cache (adds cost). We should list the impact in the checklist as a pricing delta so procurement can make a tradeoff.

I added two short comments in the UTA draft (track changes suggested) about liability caps and subprocessors; Laura, can you surface those sections to procurement as areas customers typically redline?

Markus Klein
Lead Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
